Acceptance criteria (must be verified by downstream implementation/QA):
1. Project scaffolding: A Blazor WebAssembly PWA project scaffold exists with solution and project files under the Run folder (see Run folder above) or in the managed output root when external mutation is not performed.
2. Build: dotnet build completes successfully for the solution (no compile errors) targeting .NET version agreed in downstream implementation (recorded during implementation).
3. Publish: dotnet publish (or equivalent) produces a deployable static site (wwwroot) under the Run folder with index.html, assets, and a service worker registration.
4. PWA: Web manifest (manifest.json) and service worker are present and configured so the app is installable with a basic offline shell (caching core assets). If service worker strategies are manual, document cache strategy used.
5. Runtime: Loading index.html in a static host serves the client app; main route (/) renders the app shell and additional routes (see Routes) render without server-side rendering.
6. Client-only behavior: No server-side rendering or server-side prerendering is required; app runs entirely in the browser and uses browser storage for persistence (localStorage/IndexedDB) per project notes.
7. Basic game routes/screens present and reachable by URL navigation and client router (see Routes).
8. Evidence: Build logs, publish output listing, a screenshot of the loaded app shell, browser console logs showing no uncaught exceptions at load, service worker registration log, and a short validation self-review must be written to the evidence writeback targets.

Routes / UI surfaces (minimum expected, keep generic):
- /            — App shell / landing screen
- /game        — Primary game screen (canvas or SVG rendering surface)
- /score       — Local high-score or scoreboard screen
- /about       — Minimal about/help screen (optional)

Backend / API expectations:
- This delivery is scoped as a client-only Blazor WebAssembly PWA. No server-side API implementation is included in this delivery unless downstream requirements explicitly request it.
- If a backend API is later required, list expected endpoints, authentication, and CORS expectations in a separate integration contract; not in scope here.

Exclusions (explicit):
- Server-side rendering (Blazor Server or SSR) is excluded.
- Server-side API implementation, hosting provisioning, TLS/certificate issuance, and CD pipeline setup are out of scope.
- Production performance tuning, analytics integration, and third-party telemetry onboarding are out of scope unless separately requested.

Evidence writeback targets (managed workspace paths):

- Blazor runtime evidence pack (validation artifacts): artifacts/process-runs/9bbc0667-9d12-4506-ba81-654ef924cad6/03-blazor-runtime-evidence-pack.md
- Validation self-review summary: artifacts/process-runs/9bbc0667-9d12-4506-ba81-654ef924cad6/03-validation-self-review-summary.md

Assumptions and open questions to resolve during implementation (recorded here for downstream agents):
- .NET target framework/version is unspecified; downstream implementer will choose an LTS or agreed version (e.g., .NET 8) and record it in commit notes.
- App icons and branding assets are not provided; placeholder icons will be used until provided.
- No external hosting target was provisioned in project structure; packaging will produce static-site artifacts for later static hosting.

Next actions (recommended):
1. Scaffold the Blazor WebAssembly PWA project in the Run folder using dotnet new blazorwasm --pwa (or in managed output root when mutation of external product root is not permitted). Record applied template command and created files in the runtime evidence pack.
2. Implement minimal routes and UI placeholders for the screens listed in Routes.
3. Run dotnet build and dotnet publish; collect build logs and publish output listing into the runtime evidence pack.
4. Capture at least one screenshot of the loaded app shell and client console logs; include these in the runtime evidence pack.
5. Produce the validation self-review summarizing acceptance criteria verification and link it to the Blazor runtime evidence pack node in project structure.
